title: Construction of the affine chart functor with ring and point formulas
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, $A$ a commutative ring, $i:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and $x_U:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $x=i\circ x_U$, let $p$ and $e:\kappa(p)\to\Omega$ be the point and residue embedding of $x_U$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $K$ be the separable closure of $\kappa(p)$ in $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure], with inclusion $\chi:\kappa(p)\to K$. Let $\mathcal N_U$ be the full subcategory of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods of $x$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods] whose structure map factors through $i$. Put $\mathcal T=\operatorname{EtaleResidueTriples}(A,p,K,\chi)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-residue-triples], let $D_U:\mathcal N_U^{op}\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ be global sections and $D_T:\mathcal T\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ the ring diagram. Here $\operatorname{Spec}$ and its anti-equivalence on affine schemes are as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and etale morphisms are as in [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume that each residue embedding of an object of $\mathcal N_U$ into $\Omega$ has image in $K$. There exist a functor $H:\mathcal N_U^{op}\to\mathcal T$ and a natural ring isomorphism $\delta:D_U\cong H\circ D_T$ satisfying the following formulas. For $c=(V,\bar v)$ and $t=H(c)$, require that every factorization $g:V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the structure map satisfies $\delta_c\circ g^*=\alpha_t$, where $g^*:A\to\Gamma(V)$ uses the canonical spectrum/global-sections identification. Also require that $\bar v$ followed by $V\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(V)$ equals the spectrum map of $B_t\to\kappa(q_t)\to K\to\Omega$ followed by $\operatorname{Spec}(\delta_c)$.

proof.text: Choose the chart factorization g supplied by the full-subcategory property. Cancel the monomorphism i to prove it is unique and that the pointed-neighbourhood point followed by g equals x_U. Restrict the original residue embedding to K using RingHom.codRestrict, and use SpecToEquivOfField.symm to construct a point y_c: Spec K → V_c. Its extension along K → Ω is the original geometric point. Maps from Spec K to an affine spectrum are determined after extension to Ω: use Spec.map_surjective, Spec.map_inj, and injectivity of the field map. This gives y_c followed by g equal to the base point defined by χ.

Set B_c=Γ(V_c), α_c=(ΓSpecIso A).inv followed by g.appTop, and obtain (q_c,φ_c) by applying SpecToEquivOfField K to y_c followed by V_c.toSpecΓ. Naturality of toSpecΓ identifies Spec α_c with g through the affine isomorphism V_c ≅ Spec Γ(V_c). Etale.of_comp cancels i to prove g is etale, so Spec α_c is etale. Evaluate the equation for y_c followed by g at the closed point of Spec K to prove q_c lies over p. The identity fromSpecResidueField followed by toSpecΓ = Spec Γevaluation and faithfulness of Spec translate that same equation into the compatibility of α_c and φ_c. These are the fields of the explicitly constructed triple t_c. Extending y_c back to Ω proves the required point formula.

For a neighbourhood morphism f:c→d, cancellation of i proves f followed by g_d equals g_c. Taking global sections proves α_d followed by f.appTop equals α_c. The category-of-elements condition gives commutation of the geometric points. Naturality of toSpecΓ and the point formulas then give equality of the ring maps into Ω; injectivity of K→Ω, expressed by the affine-point cancellation lemma, gives equality of the ring maps into K. Package f.appTop as an Over morphism, then an Under morphism, then an InducedCategory morphism t_d→t_c.

The identity and composition laws follow from those of the global-sections diagram DU, using extensionality of induced-category, Under and Over morphisms. Thus the object and morphism assignments define H. The ring diagram H followed by DT agrees with DU on objects and maps, so identity ring isomorphisms give δ via NatIso.ofComponents. The uniqueness of g proves the first required formula for every factorization; the point formula proves the second.

lean.statement:
theorem etale_chart_residue_triples_functor_construction
    (Y : Scheme.{v}) (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (A : CommRingCat.{v}) (i : Spec A ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion i]
    (xU : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec A) :
    let x := xU ≫ i
    let p := (SpecToEquivOfField Ω (Spec A) xU).1
    let F := (Spec A).residueField p
    let e := (SpecToEquivOfField Ω (Spec A) xU).2
    letI : Algebra F Ω := e.hom.toAlgebra
    let K := separableClosure F Ω
    let χ : F ⟶ CommRingCat.of K := CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap F K)
    let Nall := (pointSmallEtale x).fiber.Elements
    let P : ObjectProperty Nall := fun c ↦ IsAffine c.1.left
    let N := P.FullSubcategory
    let Q : ObjectProperty N := fun c ↦ ∃ g : c.obj.1.left ⟶ Spec A, g ≫ i = c.obj.1.hom
    let NU := Q.FullSubcategory
    let D := (P.ι ⋙ CategoryOfElements.π (pointSmallEtale x).fiber ⋙
      Etale.forget Y ⋙ Over.forget Y).op ⋙ Scheme.Γ
    let DU := Q.ι.op ⋙ D
    let T := EtaleResidueTriples A p K χ
    let DT := etaleResidueTriplesRingDiagram A p K χ
    (∀ (c : NU) (z : c.obj.obj.1.left.residueField
          (SpecToEquivOfField Ω c.obj.obj.1.left c.obj.obj.2.left).1),
        (SpecToEquivOfField Ω c.obj.obj.1.left c.obj.obj.2.left).2 z ∈ K) →
      ∃ (H : NUᵒᵖ ⥤ T) (δ : DU ≅ H ⋙ DT),
        (∀ c : NU,
          let t := H.obj (op c)
          (∀ g : c.obj.obj.1.left ⟶ Spec A, g ≫ i = c.obj.obj.1.hom →
            (ΓSpecIso A).inv ≫ g.appTop ≫ δ.hom.app (op c) = t.α) ∧
          c.obj.obj.2.left ≫ c.obj.obj.1.left.toSpecΓ =
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom K.subtype) ≫
              Spec.map ((ΓSpecIso t.B).inv ≫ (Spec t.B).Γevaluation t.q ≫ t.φ) ≫
              Spec.map (δ.hom.app (op c)))
